topic: Henry Tandey, Britain's most decorated WWI private, and the disputed legend that he spared a young Hitler's life
title: The WWI Soldier Who May Have Spared Hitler's Life
description: The strange, disputed WWI story of Henry Tandey, Britain's most decorated private soldier, and the wounded man he chose not to shoot. Original AI-narrated history commentary.

hook_candidates.text: What if one soldier could have shot Hitler, and simply chose not to?
A British soldier once had Hitler in his rifle sights and didn't pull the trigger.
The most decorated British private of World War One almost certainly never actually saved Hitler's life.
In 1918 a wounded, exhausted German soldier just walked past a British rifleman already aiming at him.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to their friend obsessed with what-if history because they want to argue about whether one bullet could have changed everything.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume any soldier who had Hitler in his rifle sights would have simply pulled the trigger and shot him.
closing_comment: Whether or not the soldier really spared Hitler's life, Tandey earned every one of his medals.

sources.note: Confirms Tandey's WWI decorations, the Hitler-sparing legend, and his post-war life as a factory commissionaire.
Details the 1937 Chamberlain visit and the Bavarian archive records that cast doubt on the story.
